common.unknown_reason: The box answered "{reason}", which this page does not know. Try again; if it happens again, download the diagnostic file and send it to {support}.
common.no_answer: The box did not answer. Check that your device is on the same network as the box and that the box is powered on, then try again.
common.not_served: This box does not offer this function. Update the box software, or ask {support}.
common.box_error: The box could not do this. Try again; if it happens again, download the diagnostic file and send it to {support}.
common.failed: The box could not do this. Try again; if it happens again, download the diagnostic file and send it to {support}.
common.locked: Nothing was changed: this change needs the settings code of the box. Try again and type the code.
common.other_site: This page was opened from another web site, so the box refuses the change. Open the box page at the box's own address and try again.
header.candidate: Candidate software - not for production use
offline.title: This page cannot reach the box.
offline.todo: Check that your device is on the same network as the box and that the box is powered on. The page tries again by itself.
button.set_clock: Set the clock from the server
button.own_certificate_off: Use the box's own certificate again
selftest.title: Self-test
logs.title: Viindoo IoT Box - Log
logs.heading: IoT Box - Log
logs.needs_javascript: This page needs JavaScript to read the log of the box.
selftest.summary_warning: {count} line(s) need your attention. Each tells you what to do.
selftest.summary_failed: {count} line(s) need your attention. Each tells you what to do.
selftest.summary_pending: The box is still checking {count} line(s).
selftest.hide_all: Hide the checks that are fine
reason.unknown: The box reports "{reason}" for this line, which this page does not know. Download the diagnostic file and send it to support.
reason.box_error: The box could not work out this line.
reason.network.wired: The box is on the wired network (address {address}).
reason.network.other: The box has the network address {address}.
reason.network.no_address: The box has no network address.
reason.network.link_local_only: The box gave itself an address because no router answered.
reason.network.access_point: The box has its own Wi-Fi network and is not on yours yet.
reason.network.no_gateway: The box has an address but no gateway, so it cannot reach other networks.
action.connect_network: Plug in a network cable, or choose a Wi-Fi network under Network.
action.check_dhcp: Check that the router hands out addresses (DHCP) on this port, then restart the box.
action.join_wifi: Choose your Wi-Fi network under Network, or plug in a network cable.
action.check_router: Check that the router gives the box a gateway (default route).
reason.name_resolution.no_server: No server yet, so there is no name to look up.
reason.name_resolution.address_given: The server is given as an address, so there is no name to look up.
reason.name_resolution.no_such_name: The network does not know the server name.
reason.name_resolution.no_answer: The network did not answer the question for the server name.
action.check_server_address: Check the server address you typed when connecting; a typing mistake is the usual cause.
action.check_dns: Check that the box reaches the internet and that the name service of the router works, then look again in a minute.
reason.clock.synchronised: The clock is kept by a time server.
reason.clock.agrees_with_server: The clock agrees with the clock of the server.
reason.clock.unknown: The box cannot tell whether its clock is right.
reason.clock.not_synchronised: No time server keeps the clock of the box. The board has no battery clock, so the time may be wrong after a power cut.
reason.clock.wrong: The clock of the box is wrong by about {minutes} minute(s), so secure connections fail.
reason.clock.server_clock_differs: The box follows a time server, but the clock of the server differs by about {minutes} minute(s).
action.allow_time_server: Let the box reach a time server (UDP port 123) on your network, or set the clock from the server.
action.set_clock_from_server: Set the clock of the box from the server.
action.check_server_clock: Ask the administrator of the server to correct the clock of the server.
reason.server.no_server: The box is not connected to a server.
reason.server.not_resolved: The name of the server {server} cannot be resolved.
reason.server.timeout: The server {server} did not answer in time.
reason.server.no_route: There is no route from the box to the server {server}.
reason.server.not_http: {server} did not answer like a web server.
reason.server.box_error: The box could not check the server.
action.check_network_firewall: Check the server address, the firewall and the proxy between the box and the server.
reason.certificate.no_server: No server, so there is no certificate to check.
reason.certificate.not_https: The server is reached without encryption (http).
reason.certificate.checking: Checking the certificate of the server...
reason.certificate.not_checked: The certificate of the server was not checked.
reason.certificate.public: The certificate of the server is issued by a public authority.
reason.certificate.trusted_by_you: The certificate of the server is the one you confirmed when connecting.
reason.certificate.box_clock: The certificate of the server looks out of date, but the clock of the box is wrong.
reason.certificate.expired: The certificate of the server has expired.
reason.certificate.not_yet_valid: The certificate of the server is not valid yet.
reason.certificate.name_mismatch: The certificate of the server was issued for another name than the address used.
reason.certificate.changed: The certificate of the server is not the one you confirmed: it has changed.
reason.certificate.untrusted: The certificate of the server is not issued by a public authority and was never confirmed.
reason.certificate.invalid: The certificate of the server is not valid.
action.use_https: Use an https address if the server offers one.
action.renew_server_certificate: Ask the administrator of the server to renew the certificate.
action.pair_again: Connect the box again with a new pairing code and confirm the certificate. If you did not expect this change, do not connect and tell the administrator of the server.
action.reset_then_pair: If the record of this box in Viindoo was archived, unarchive it: the server then accepts the box again and nothing else is needed. Otherwise the settings code this box asks for can no longer be read anywhere, so reset the box with the reset file: switch the box off, take out its card and put the card in a computer, open the partition the computer shows and create an empty file named viindoo-reset (or viindoo-reset.txt) at the top of it, then put the card back and start the box. The box forgets its server and its lock. Then pair it with a new code from the server: on the record of this box choose Re-pair, or choose Connect an IoT Box to connect it as a new box, and use that code with Connect here.
action.restart_for_name: Nothing to do now: browsers reach the box by its address with its own certificate, and the box checks its Viindoo name again by itself. If this stays for a day, restart the box; if it still stays, download the diagnostic file and send it to {support}.
reason.registration.not_paired: The box is not connected to a server yet.
reason.registration.accepted: The server accepted this box at {when} and takes its reports.
reason.registration.accepted_no_time: The server knows this box and takes its reports.
reason.registration.refused: The server no longer knows this box: its record was archived or deleted, or a Re-pair code for it was used.
reason.registration.unreachable: The box cannot send its reports to the server.
reason.registration.not_yet: The box has just started and has not registered yet.
reason.registration.never: The box has not managed to register since it started.
action.pair_box: Connect the box: choose Connect under Server and use a pairing link or code from Viindoo.
action.check_server: Check the Server line: the server must be running and have the IoT app installed. If this stays, restart the box.
reason.live_channel.no_server: No server, so no live channel.
reason.live_channel.connected: The live channel to the server has been open since {when}.
reason.live_channel.connected_no_time: The live channel to the server is open.
reason.live_channel.connecting: The box is opening the live channel to the server...
reason.live_channel.reconnecting: The live channel was lost at {when}; the box keeps trying to open it again.
reason.live_channel.reconnecting_no_time: The live channel was lost; the box keeps trying to open it again.
reason.live_channel.waiting: The live channel waits for the server to accept the box.
action.check_registration: Look at the Registration line and do what it says.
action.restart_box: Restart the box. If this stays, contact support.
reason.browser_address.own_name: Browsers are given the name you set: {address}.
reason.browser_address.viindoo_name: Browsers are given the Viindoo name {address}.
reason.browser_address.name: Browsers are given the name {address}.
reason.browser_address.certificate_box: with the box's own certificate, which each browser accepts once
reason.browser_address.certificate_viind: with its Viindoo certificate, which browsers trust without a warning
reason.browser_address.no_address: The box has no usable address to give to browsers.
reason.browser_address.link_local: The only address of the box was chosen by the box itself, so other computers cannot count on it.
reason.browser_address.no_certificate: The box has no certificate for secure connections from browsers.
reason.browser_address.shared_certificat: The box uses the certificate that every unmodified box shares.
reason.browser_address.certificate_expir: The certificate that browsers get from the box has expired.
reason.browser_address.local_name: The box has no address on your network, so browsers are given its local name {address}, which some networks do not resolve.
reason.browser_address.certificate_not_f: The certificate of the box was not issued for {address}, so browsers will warn.
reason.browser_address.certificate_being: The address of the box changed and the box is making a certificate for it, which takes a few seconds. Afterwards each browser that accepted the earlier certificate of the box accepts the new one once.
reason.browser_address.certificate_not_s: The box made itself a new certificate, but its web server still serves the earlier one, so browsers do not get the new one yet.
reason.browser_address.certificate_endin: The certificate that browsers get from the box ends on {date}.
reason.browser_address.address_certifica: The certificate that browsers get when they open the box by its address has expired. Browsers given the Viindoo name {address} are not affected.
The certificate that browsers get when they open the box by its address ends on {date}. Browsers given the Viindoo name {address} are not affected.
reason.browser_address.name_certificate_: Browsers are given the Viindoo name {address}, but the box cannot read the certificate of that name, so it cannot tell whether browsers trust it.
reason.browser_address.accept_again: Browsers that accepted an earlier certificate of this box ask once more: accept this one once in each of them.
action.renew_own_certificate: Install a new certificate for this box under Advanced, Certificate.
reason.viindoo_name.own_certificate: You installed your own certificate, so the box does not ask for a Viindoo name.
reason.viindoo_name.own_name: Browsers are still given the name you set for your own certificate, now with a certificate the box made itself, so the box does not ask for a Viindoo name. The box forgets that name when it leaves its server with Disconnect or is reset with the reset file.
reason.viindoo_name.not_offered: This server does not offer a Viindoo name.
reason.viindoo_name.disabled: The Viindoo name is switched off in Viindoo.
reason.viindoo_name.no_answer_yet: The box asked for a Viindoo name and has no answer yet. It asks again by itself.
reason.viindoo_name.certificate_on_its_w: The box has the Viindoo name {name}; its certificate is being made.
reason.viindoo_name.address_not_private: The addresses of this site are not private ones, so no Viindoo name is given.
reason.viindoo_name.limit_reached: This database has all the Viindoo names it may have.
reason.viindoo_name.try_later: Too many certificates were made for this box this week. The box asks again later.
reason.viindoo_name.refused: The server refused to give a Viindoo name ({server_reason}).
reason.viindoo_name.box_clock_wrong: The clock of the box is wrong, so it cannot install its Viindoo name.
reason.viindoo_name.authorities_out_of_d: The box could not install its Viindoo name; its list of trusted certificate authorities may be out of date.
reason.viindoo_name.validity_unconfirmed: The dates of the certificate of the Viindoo name look wrong, but the server gave no time, so the box cannot tell whether its clock or the certificate is at fault.
reason.viindoo_name.not_installed: The box could not install its Viindoo name ({problem}).
reason.viindoo_name.network_refuses_name: This network does not accept the name {name}.
reason.viindoo_name.name_check_failed: The box could not confirm that it is reached by the name {name} ({check}).
reason.viindoo_name.expired: The certificate of the Viindoo name has expired. Meanwhile the box uses its own certificate and keeps asking the server for a new one.
reason.viindoo_name.renewal_retrying: The certificate of the Viindoo name ends on {date}; renewal is being retried.
reason.viindoo_name.checking_name: The box is checking that its Viindoo name works.
reason.viindoo_name.in_use: The box is reached by its Viindoo name {name}.
reason.viindoo_name.box_unknown: The Viindoo server no longer knows this box, so it gives no Viindoo name.
reason.viindoo_name.waiting_for_address: The box waits for a network address before it asks for its Viindoo name.
action.use_own_certificate: Install your own certificate under Advanced, Certificate, or accept the box once in each browser.
action.ask_administrator: Ask the administrator of the database to contact Viindoo support or to archive the boxes no longer used.
action.allow_zone: Ask the network administrator to allow the zone {zone} on the name service of the router. Until then the box keeps working with its own certificate.
reason.software.no_release: The box cannot tell which release of the software it runs.
reason.software.up_to_date: The box software is the latest release.
reason.software.applied: The latest release was just applied.
reason.software.trial: A new release is on trial after a restart; the box keeps it once it runs well.
reason.software.checking: The box is looking for a new release...
reason.software.applying: The box is applying a release and restarts.
reason.software.unreachable: The box could not reach the place where releases are published. Updates need internet access; devices work without it. Look again when the network is back.
reason.software.no_channel: The box found no release channel to follow, so it keeps the release it runs.
reason.software.no_pointer: No release is published yet for this box, so it keeps the release it runs.
reason.software.release_untagged: The release channel names no published release; nothing was changed.
reason.software.candidate_refused: The release that is published is a candidate, which this box does not install. It keeps the release it runs.
reason.software.not_checked: The box has not looked for a new release yet.
reason.software.pointer_invalid: The information about the published release cannot be read. The box keeps the release it runs; look again later, and contact support if this stays.
reason.software.needs_new_image: The new release needs a newer image of the box than the one on its card.
reason.software.core_commit_unavailable: The new release needs software that could not be downloaded. The box keeps the release it runs; look again later.
reason.software.bad_release: A release was tried on this box and undone because it did not run well; it will not be applied again. The box keeps its working release. Contact support.
reason.software.apply_failed: Applying the release failed; the box kept its working release. Look again later, and contact support if it fails again.
action.apply_update: Choose Update to {offered} under Software. The box restarts.
action.apply_update_no_release: Choose the button that starts with Update to, under Software. The box restarts.
action.write_new_image: Write a newer image to the card of the box, as the guide says; the box cannot update itself this time.
reason.devices.none: No device is connected yet. Plug a device in: it appears under Devices within seconds (printers within two minutes).
reason.drivers.failed_to_load: Some device drivers could not be loaded: {files}.
reason.layer.in_place: The box software is in place.
reason.layer.starting: The box software is still starting...
reason.layer.load_order: The box software did not start in the right order.
reason.layer.not_in_place: Part of the box software is not in place.
action.contact_support: Download the diagnostic file and send it to {support}.
action.unknown: Download the diagnostic file and send it to {support}.
server.title: Server
server.settings_open: Open: the box has no server, so no code is needed.
server.settings_locked: Locked: a change asks for the settings code that the administrators read on the box record in Viindoo.
server.not_connected: The box is not connected to a server.
server.how_1: In Viindoo, open the IoT app and choose Connect an IoT Box.
server.how_2: Copy the pairing link that Viindoo shows, or note the address of the server and the pairing code.
server.how_3: Choose Connect here and paste the link, or type the address and the code.
server.kinds: The server can be Viindoo Cloud, or your own Viindoo server.
network.title: Network
network.kind_access_point: Own Wi-Fi network of the box
devices.title: Devices
devices.none: No device is connected yet. Plug a device in: it appears here within seconds (printers within two minutes).
device.why_command_set: Taken for this kind of printer because the printer announces the command language {evidence}.
device.why_name: Taken for this kind of printer because its name contains "{evidence}".
device.why_default: Taken for an office printer because nothing says it is a receipt or a label printer.
device.protocol: Protocol read by the box: {name} ({baudrate} baud).
device.print_test_waiting: Waiting for the printer to take the test (up to 30 seconds)...
device.test_taken: The printer took the test. Check that the page came out.
device.listening: Listening for {seconds} seconds. Scan a barcode or press a key now; what you do appears below.
device.listen_shared: The device is not taken from the station that uses it: what you scan or press is also received there.
device.listen_help: Choose Listen, then scan or press: you see what the box receives from this device.
device.nothing_heard: Nothing was received from this device.
device.nothing_heard_todo: Scan or press again while the page listens. If still nothing arrives, unplug the device and plug it in again.
device.switched: This device is now used as: {kind}.
device.label_added: A print queue named {queue} was added for this printer. The printer keeps working through its current queue, and it also appears as a label printer within two minutes.
device.label_exists: Already set up as a label printer through the print queue {queue}.
device.display_help: The screen shows the identification page of the box until a till or a station uses it.
device.weight_no_unit: The scale reads {value}, in the unit set on the scale; compare it with the scale's display.
device.test.not_connected: This device is not connected any more.
device.test.test_in_progress: A test of this device is already running.
device.test.timeout: The device did not answer in time.
device.test.print_server_silent: The print server of the box did not answer, so the test could not finish.
device.test.device_error: The device failed during the test.
device.test.queue_missing: The print queue of this printer is missing.
device.test.queue_not_accepting: The print queue does not accept jobs: the printer is stopped.
device.test.not_queued: The test did not reach the print queue.
device.test.job_aborted: The print job was aborted by the printer.
device.test.printer_not_reached: The printer did not take the test within 30 seconds, so the test was cancelled.
device.test.printer_not_reached_network: The printer at {address} did not answer within 30 seconds, so the test was cancelled.
device.test.sent_not_followed: The test was sent to the printer, but the box could not follow it, so it cannot tell whether the printer took it.
device.test.tested_by_page: This device is tested with Listen.
device.test.shows_identification_page: A screen is tested by looking at it: it shows the identification page of the box.
device.test_todo.not_connected: Plug the device in again and wait a few seconds.
device.test_todo.test_in_progress: Wait a moment and try again.
device.test_todo.timeout: Check the cable and the power of the device, then try again.
device.test_todo.print_server_silent: Restart the box, then try again.
device.test_todo.device_error: Unplug the device, plug it in again and try again.
device.test_todo.queue_missing: Unplug the printer, plug it in again and wait two minutes.
device.test_todo.queue_not_accepting: Check that the printer is on, has paper and no error light, then try again.
device.test_todo.not_queued: Try again; if it fails again, restart the box.
device.test_todo.job_stopped: Check the paper and the cover of the printer, then try again.
device.test_todo.job_aborted: Check the paper, the cover and the cable of the printer, then try again.
device.test_todo.printer_not_reached: Check that the printer is switched on, has paper, and that its USB cable is plugged in.
device.test_todo.printer_not_reached_net: Check that the printer is switched on and connected to the network, and that {address} is still its address; if the router gave it a new one, add the printer again with the new address.
device.test_todo.printer_not_reached_unk: Check that the printer is switched on, has paper and is connected by its cable or to the network, then try again.
device.test_todo.sent_not_followed: Look at the printer: check whether the page came out.
device.test_todo.no_reading: Put a weight on the scale and check its cable and its serial settings; if the scale has a menu, choose the protocol the manual names.
device.listen_failed.no_answer: The box stopped answering while listening.
device.use_as.not_connected: This device is not connected any more.
device.use_as.invalid_choice: The choice was not understood. Reload the page and try again.
device.label.not_connected: This printer is not connected any more. Plug it in again and wait a few seconds.
device.label.not_office_printer: Only an office printer can be made a label printer.
device.label.queue_missing: The print queue of this printer is missing. Unplug the printer, plug it in again and wait two minutes.
device.label.already_added: This printer already stands as a label printer through the print queue {queue}. Nothing was added.
printer.title: Add a network printer
printer.intro: Use this for a printer on your network that takes raw jobs (usually on port 9100) and does not announce itself. The box then treats it like a printer plugged in.
printer.address_help: An address or a host name, with a port if it is not 9100.
printer.name: Name (optional)
printer.name_help: Letters, digits, hyphen and underscore. Leave empty to name it after its address.
printer.added: The printer was added with the print queue {queue}.
printer.appears: It appears under Devices within {seconds} seconds. Then use Print test.
printer.invalid_kind: The kind of printer was not understood. Choose one from the list.
printer.invalid_address: This is not an address of a printer. Type an IP address or a host name of the printer, for example 192.168.1.50.
printer.invalid_name: This name does not fit the kind of printer you chose. Use another name, or leave the name empty.
printer.already_added: The box already has a print queue for this address: {queue}. Look for it under Devices.
printer.print_server_unavailable: The print service of the box is not running. Restart the box and try again.
printer.print_server_error: The print service refused the printer. Check the address, then try again; if it happens again, send the diagnostic file to support.
software.title: Software
software.auto_help: A new release is applied by itself, and the box restarts. Turn it off to update only when you choose Update.
software.rolled_back: The release {release} was tried and undone because it did not run well. The box keeps the release that works.
update.invalid_action: The box did not understand the request. Reload the page and try again.
update.invalid_choice: The choice was not understood. Reload the page and try again.
advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.locked_help: On a box connected to a server, the changes in this panel ask for the settings code that the administrators read on the box record in Viindoo.
certificate.subject: Subject
viindoo_name.name: Viindoo name
address.kind_own_name: The name you set when you installed your own certificate
address.kind_local_name: The local name of the box
address.help: This is the address that Viindoo gives to the browsers of your users to reach the box. A browser accepts the certificate of the box once per box and per address.
identity.name: Name of the box
identity.name_help: This name stays with the box for its whole life. To give it a name your team recognises, set its Box Name on the box form in Viindoo.
unlock.title: Settings code
unlock.explain: This box is connected to a server, so changes to it need the settings code. It proves that you are allowed to change this box.
unlock.label: Settings code
unlock.where: In Viindoo, an administrator opens the record of this box and reads the settings code there.
unlock.no_code: If nobody can read the settings code, or the code on the box record is refused, reset the box: switch it off, put its card in a computer, create an empty file named viindoo-reset at the top of the partition the computer shows, then put the card back and start the box. It forgets its server and its lock, and you pair it with a new code.
unlock.invalid_code: This is not the settings code of this box. Read it again on the record of this box in Viindoo; after the box was paired again, the previous code no longer works.
pair.title: Connect the box to a server
pair.intro: Paste the pairing link from Viindoo, or type the address of the server and the pairing code. The code works once and for 15 minutes.
pair.link_help: Viindoo shows the link when you choose Connect an IoT Box. Paste all of it, including the part after #.
pair.server_help: The address you use to open Viindoo in your browser.
pair.code_help: Generated in Viindoo, valid once and for 15 minutes.
pair.insecure: This address starts with http: what the box and the server exchange is not encrypted. Use https if the server has it.
pair.invalid_link.title: This is not a pairing link.
pair.invalid_link.todo: Paste the whole link from Viindoo, or choose Address and code and type them separately.
pair.code_missing.title: No pairing code was typed.
pair.code_missing.todo: Type the code that Viindoo shows.
pair.invalid_address.title: The address of the server is not an address.
pair.invalid_address.todo: Correct it, for example https://erp.example.com, without anything after the name of the server.
pair.invalid_authority.title: The certificate you pasted cannot be read.
pair.invalid_authority.todo: Paste the certificate of your authority as text, from -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- to -----END CERTIFICATE-----.
pair.authority_not_root.title: The certificate you pasted is not the root of an authority.
pair.authority_not_root.todo: Paste the root certificate of the authority that issued the certificate of your server.
pair.server_not_found.title: The name of the server cannot be resolved.
pair.server_not_found.todo: Check the address, and check that the box reaches the internet (see the self-test).
pair.server_unreachable.title: The server does not answer.
pair.server_unreachable.todo: Check the address, the firewall and the proxy between the box and the server.
pair.server_not_compatible.title: This server does not offer pairing for Viindoo IoT boxes.
pair.server_not_compatible.todo: The address may be wrong, the IoT app may not be installed there, or the server serves several databases and none is selected.
pair.invalid_code.title: The server does not know this code.
pair.invalid_code.todo: Generate a new code in Viindoo and copy it exactly.
pair.expired.title: This code is too old.
pair.expired.todo: Generate a new code in Viindoo; a code works for 15 minutes.
pair.already_used.title: This code was already used.
pair.already_used.todo: Generate a new code in Viindoo.
pair.identifier_exists.title: This box is already registered as {box_name}.
pair.identifier_exists.todo: In Viindoo, open that box and use Re-pair, then use the new code here.
pair.identifier_exists_other.title: This box is already registered in this database, under another company.
pair.identifier_exists_other.todo: Ask an administrator of the database.
pair.server_error.title: The server could not complete the pairing.
pair.server_error.todo: Try again with the same code. If it happens again, the administrator of the server reads the log of the server.
pair.unknown_reason.title: The server refused the pairing ({server_reason}).
pair.unknown_reason.todo: Update the box, or ask support and give them that word.
pair.box_error.title: The box could not complete the pairing.
pair.box_error.todo: Try again in a moment. If it happens again, download the diagnostic file and send it to support.
pair.locked.title: Nothing was changed: the box needs its settings code.
pair.locked.todo: Choose Connect again and type the settings code from the record of this box in Viindoo.
pair.box_clock_wrong.title: The clock of the box is wrong, so secure connections fail.
pair.box_clock_wrong.todo: Set the clock of the box from the server, or let the box reach a time server (UDP port 123), then connect again.
pair.problem_unknown_authority: The certificate of the server is not issued by a public authority.
pair.problem_private_authority: The certificate of the server was issued by an authority of your own organization.
pair.problem_name_mismatch: The certificate of the server was issued for another name than this address.
pair.problem_expired: The certificate of the server has expired.
pair.problem_not_yet_valid: The certificate of the server is not valid yet.
pair.problem_invalid: The certificate of the server is not valid.
pair.trust_explain: Compare the fingerprint below with the one the administrator of the server gives you. Only if they are the same, trust this certificate. It is trusted for this server and nothing else.
pair.trust_help: If the fingerprint is not the same, do not trust it and tell the administrator of the server.
pair.private_authority: This one certificate cannot be trusted by itself. Paste the root certificate of your authority below and confirm its fingerprint, or ask for a certificate from a public authority.
pair.untrusted_todo: This certificate cannot be trusted from here. Ask the administrator of the server to fix the certificate, and check the address you typed.
pair.authority_help: Paste it as text, from -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- to -----END CERTIFICATE-----.
clock.title: Clock of the box
clock.explain: The board of the box has no battery clock. When the clock is wrong, secure connections fail. Here you compare it with the clock of the server and, if you choose, set it.
clock.reading: Reading the clock of the server...
clock.unverified: The identity of this server was not checked. Compare its time with a clock you trust before setting the box.
clock.synchronised: A time server already keeps the clock of the box; it is not set by hand.
clock.set: Set the clock of the box to this time
clock.done: The clock of the box is set.
clock.server_missing: Type the address of the server to read its clock.
clock.invalid_address: The address of the server is not an address. Correct it and try again.
clock.other_server: This is not the server of the box. Use the address of the server the box is connected to.
clock.server_not_found: The name of the server cannot be resolved. Check the address and the internet access of the box.
clock.server_unreachable: The server does not answer. Check the address, the firewall and the proxy.
clock.server_certificate_untrusted: The certificate of the server cannot be checked, so its time is not read. Connect the box first and confirm the certificate, or use a server with a public certificate.
clock.no_time: The server did not tell the time. Try another address of the same server, or set the time by another way.
clock.clock_synchronised: A time server already keeps the clock of the box.
disconnect.title: Disconnect the box from its server
disconnect.explain: The box forgets its server and the credential it uses for it (the settings code is then no longer asked), the certificates trusted for that server and its Viindoo name, then restarts. It keeps the choice to update automatically and the Wi-Fi network. Its devices stay plugged in, but nothing reaches Viindoo until you connect the box again.
disconnect.own_name_kept: Your own certificate stays installed, and browsers are still given the name you typed for it ({name}).
disconnect.own_name_forgotten: It also forgets the name you typed earlier for your own certificate ({name}), because that certificate is no longer installed.
disconnect.record: In Viindoo the record of the box stays, shown as disconnected. If you retire the box, archive that record there.
disconnect.failed: The box could not disconnect. Try again; if it happens again, send the diagnostic file to support.
restart.title: Restart the box
restart.explain: The box software restarts. Devices and printing from Viindoo pause for about a minute, and this page waits for the box.
restart.failed: The box could not restart. Try again; if it happens again, switch the box off and on.
ssh.title: Password for shell access
ssh.explain: Technicians use this password to open a shell on the box and to open the printer administration. You only need it when support asks for it. On a box connected to a server the password lasts until the box restarts, because the box sets a new random one at every start. A box not connected to a server keeps it until you generate another.
ssh.replaces: A new password replaces the previous one.
ssh.once: Note it now: the box does not show it again.
ssh.failed: The box could not set a new password. Try again; if it happens again, send the diagnostic file to support.
restart.paired: The box is connected and restarts to finish.
restart.disconnected: The box is disconnected and restarts.
restart.update: The box looks for a release and restarts into it if it finds one.
restart.wait: This page waits for the box and shows it again by itself. Do not switch the box off.
restart.failed_title: The box does not come back.
restart.failed_todo: Wait a few more minutes, then reload the page. If the box stays away, check its power and its network cable, then switch it off and on.
restart.done_paired: Connected to {server} as {name}. The box is registering; the Server section shows Registered once the server has taken it.
restart.done_disconnected: The box is disconnected from its server. Connect it again whenever you need.
restart.done_update: The box restarted into the new release.
restart.not_restarted: The box did not restart. Look at the Software section for the state of the update.
wifi.title: Wi-Fi
wifi.intro: Choose the Wi-Fi network the box should use. Once it joins, you reach it on that network, no longer on its own network.
wifi.name: Name of the Wi-Fi network
wifi.none_found: No network was found. Type the name of the network.
wifi.password: Password (leave empty for a network without one)
wifi.keep: Keep this network after a restart
wifi.joining_todo: This page loses contact with the box. Connect your device to the same network the box joined and wait a minute.
wifi.open_by_name: On a device on that network, open the box by its name:
wifi.open_by_address: Or open the box by the address it has on that network. The box shows it on its screen, on the status ticket of a USB receipt printer, and the list of devices of your router shows it too.
wifi.failed: The box could not use this Wi-Fi network. Check the name and the password, then try again.
wifi.busy: The box is changing its Wi-Fi by itself at this moment: it is going back to the network it keeps, or starting its own network. Wait a minute, then try again.
wifi.invalid_name: This network name cannot be used: a Wi-Fi network name has 1 to 32 characters (fewer when it holds accented letters or symbols) and holds no line break, tab or other control character. Check the name and try again.
wifi.invalid_password: This password cannot be used: it holds a line break, a tab or another control character, which a Wi-Fi password does not have. Check the password and try again.
certificate.intro: Install a certificate of your organization for the box, so that browsers on your network show no warning. Type the name the certificate was issued for; browsers are then given that name for this box.
certificate.host: Name the certificate was issued for
certificate.host_help: For example box1.example.com. Your DNS must point this name to the box.
certificate.pem_help: The certificate first, then the certificates of its chain.
certificate.key_help: The key goes from this browser to the box on your network and is not kept anywhere else. Do this only on a network you trust.
certificate.installed_todo: Open the box at https://{host} to check that your browser shows no warning. The server is told the new address within moments.
certificate.restore_title: Use the certificate of the box again
certificate.restore_explain: The box makes its own certificate again and serves it instead of yours. Browsers will warn again until each accepts the box. Browsers are still given the name you typed for your certificate, and the box does not ask for a Viindoo name while it keeps that name; it forgets the name when it leaves its server with Disconnect or is reset with the reset file.
certificate.restored: The box serves its own certificate again.
certificate.invalid_certificate: The certificate cannot be read. Paste it as text, from -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- to -----END CERTIFICATE-----.
certificate.common_name_missing: The certificate has no common name, which the box needs. Ask for a certificate that has one.
certificate.invalid_key: The private key cannot be read. Paste it as text, from -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- to -----END PRIVATE KEY-----.
certificate.key_encrypted: The private key is protected by a password. Remove the password from the key, then paste it again.
certificate.key_mismatch: The key does not belong to this certificate. Paste the key that was made with the certificate request.
certificate.not_yet_valid: The certificate is not valid yet. Check the clock of the box, or the start date of the certificate.
certificate.expired: The certificate has expired. Ask for a new one.
certificate.invalid_host_name: The name is not a host name. Type a name such as box1.example.com.
certificate.host_name_mismatch: The certificate was not issued for this name. Type a name that the certificate covers.
certificate.box_error: The box could not install the certificate and keeps the one it had. Try again; if it happens again, send the diagnostic file to support.
loglevel.title: Log levels
loglevel.intro: The log of the box tells support what happened. The level {recommended} is recommended: a more detailed level makes the log long and slow to read.
loglevel.to_server: Send the log of the box to the server
loglevel.to_server_none: Send the log of the box to the server (once it is connected)
loglevel.level_not_offered: This level is not offered for the whole box: it would keep the box from stopping cleanly. Choose another level.
loglevel.failed: The level was not changed. Try again; if it happens again, send the diagnostic file to support.
